name: Buchholz-Lechner / Alazzawi-Lechner Bisognano-Wichmann
statement: Bisognano-Wichmann for wedge algebras generated by polarisation-free wedge-local fields holds only under energy or particle-number bounds on the fields, which make field products applied to the vacuum well defined
requires: energy bounds or particle-number bounds on the wedge-local fields
a core of field polynomials applied to the vacuum

name: Mund's theorem
statement: Mund: Bisognano-Wichmann follows from the particle structure (asymptotic completeness, mass gap) of a local net on double cones
requires: a local net of double-cone algebras

name: Morinelli's theorem
statement: Morinelli: Bisognano-Wichmann from modular covariance of the one-particle net holds in spacetime dimension at least three

name: Borchers' theorem
statement: Borchers: for a Borchers triple, Delta^{it} U(x) Delta^{-it} = U(Lambda(-2 pi t) x) and J U(x) J = U(-x), so modular unitaries act like boosts and reflections on translations
requires: Omega cyclic and separating for M
U(x) M U(x)* in M for x in the wedge

name: Bisognano-Wichmann from asymptotic completeness
statement: A unitary fixing Omega, commuting with translations, preserving M and acting as 1 on H_1 fixes every Haag-Ruelle scattering state; applied to V(t) = U(0,-2 pi t) Delta^{-it} and J_M J it gives Bisognano-Wichmann on the scattering states, hence on all of H under asymptotic completeness

name: Bisognano-Wichmann as standard subspaces
statement: For a Borchers triple, Bisognano-Wichmann holds iff the standard subspace H_M is contained in the free standard subspace H_0, iff {S_M = S_0} is dense

name: Wedge duality from Bisognano-Wichmann
statement: Either half of Bisognano-Wichmann (Delta or J) gives wedge duality M' = J M J

name: Reeh-Schlieder
statement: Reeh-Schlieder: the vacuum is cyclic for every local algebra of a region with non-empty causal complement

name: Modular nuclearity implies split
statement: Buchholz-D'Antoni-Longo / Buchholz-Lechner: nuclearity of M(x) -> Delta^{1/4} A Omega, with Delta the modular operator of the larger algebra, gives the split property for the inclusion M(x) in M
requires: Delta equal to the free Delta_0, i.e. Bisognano-Wichmann

name: Split implies non-trivial double cones
statement: A split wedge inclusion with factorial algebras gives a relative commutant isomorphic to M(x)' tensor M, a type III factor, so the double-cone algebra is non-trivial

name: Hyperfiniteness from split
statement: Hyperfiniteness of local algebras needs the split property at arbitrarily small distances, not only at large distances

name: Kato-Rellich
statement: Kato-Rellich: A + B is self-adjoint on Dom A when A is self-adjoint and B symmetric with relative bound less than 1
requires: B relatively bounded by A with bound < 1

name: KLMN
statement: KLMN: the form sum of positive self-adjoint operators defines a self-adjoint operator extending A + B on Dom A intersected with Dom B; it does not show A + B is self-adjoint or essentially self-adjoint on the intersection

name: Basic criterion for self-adjointness
statement: A positive symmetric operator T with Ran(T + 1) equal to the whole Hilbert space is self-adjoint; dense range gives only essential self-adjointness

name: Nelson commutator theorem
statement: Nelson / Glimm-Jaffe commutator theorem: T is essentially self-adjoint on a core of a positive comparison operator N if ||Tu|| <= c ||Nu|| and |<Tu, Nu> - <Nu, Tu>| <= d ||N^{1/2}u||^2
requires: a comparison operator N >= 1 with T N-bounded

name: Strong commutation
statement: If A and B are self-adjoint and strongly commute (commuting spectral projections), A + B is essentially self-adjoint on Dom A intersected with Dom B
requires: strong commutation, not just commutation on a core

name: Stone's theorem
statement: Stone: strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups correspond exactly to self-adjoint generators

name: Haag-Ruelle scattering
statement: Haag-Ruelle scattering theory constructs asymptotic in and out states from a mass gap and isolated one-particle mass shell; for wedge-local nets Duell's version applies

name: Asymptotic completeness
statement: Asymptotic completeness: the Moller operators are unitary onto H, i.e. the scattering states span the whole Hilbert space
requires: identification of the n-particle out-states for every n

name: Lechner wedge-local construction
statement: Lechner: a two-particle S-matrix without poles in the physical strip gives polarisation-free wedge-local fields via the Zamolodchikov-Faddeev algebra and a Borchers triple
requires: S analytic and bounded in the physical strip (no bound-state poles)

name: Tanimoto bound-state construction
statement: Tanimoto: for S-matrices with bound-state poles, the fields chi(xi), chi'(eta) give a Borchers triple provided chi(xi) + chi'(eta) is essentially self-adjoint (HA-T)

name: Kinematic pole obstruction
statement: Created Zamolodchikov-Faddeev two-particle vectors are never in the domain of chi'_2 because of the kinematic pole of S at i pi/3, so products of three bound-state fields never have Omega in their domain

name: Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction
statement: Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction gives a Wightman theory from Euclidean correlation functions satisfying reflection positivity, regularity and the OS axioms; it does not identify the S-matrix

name: Modular nuclearity from analytic continuation
statement: Modular nuclearity of Xi(s) follows from geometric-in-n L2 bounds on analytic continuations of the n-particle wave functions of wedge vectors (a first-slot bound at fixed depth)
requires: an L2 bound geometric in n on the continuation (FS_geom)

name: Tomita-Takesaki
statement: Tomita-Takesaki: for M with cyclic separating Omega, S A Omega = A* Omega closes to S = J Delta^{1/2}, Delta^{it} M Delta^{-it} = M and J M J = M'

name: Weak limits and closed operators
statement: If u_k converges weakly to u and T u_k is bounded, and T is closed, then u is in Dom T and T u_k converges weakly to T u along a subsequence

name: Bounded perturbation
statement: A self-adjoint operator plus a bounded symmetric operator is self-adjoint on the same domain
